Both are letters to Senate appropriations figures attacking House-added restrictions in an appropriation bill, explaining how those restrictions would impair the defense effort and established federal policy, contrasting them with the more measured January Budget request, detailing stranded local commitments or federal investments, and closing by urging removal of the limitations and restoration of requested funds. This unusually close argumentative and operative sequence is material, not merely a shared governmental function. C05 is also close in subject and requested action but is much shorter and less structurally similar; C20 shares hydroelectric-policy concepts but pursues a different legislative objective.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"I am writing to express my deep concern over certain drastic limitations ... in H.R. 3790, the Interior Department appropriation bill ... in the form in which that bill passed the House of Representatives and is now before your subcommittee.","parent_excerpt":"I am deeply concerned about the crippling limitation ... which the House included in H.R. 3880, the Independent Offices Appropriation Bill. ... I earnestly hope the limitation can be removed before the Congress completes action on this bill.","explanation":"Both open by identifying a damaging House-imposed limitation in an appropriation bill now subject to Senate review."},{"child_excerpt":"Taken together, these amendments would seriously restrict the operation of Federal hydroelectric power projects for the national defense and in the public interest.","parent_excerpt":"This will have an adverse effect on our defense effort.","explanation":"Each immediately frames the appropriation restriction as harmful to defense mobilization."},{"child_excerpt":"Funds were included in the January Budget for transmission lines only in cases where they are urgently needed ... And yet they were slashed--on the House floor","parent_excerpt":"In the January budget, funds were requested for only 75,000 new units in fiscal 1952. ... Yet, that is exactly what this bill will do.","explanation":"Both defend a deliberately limited January Budget request against a more drastic House-floor restriction."},{"child_excerpt":"This project is already sixty percent completed, at a cost so far of nearly $3 million. This money will be entirely wasted ... if construction is now stopped for lack of further funds.","parent_excerpt":"A great many communities have made plans and committed funds ... Sites have already been purchased for nearly 63,000 of these units. If the limitations of the House bill are allowed to stand, virtually none of them could be built next year.","explanation":"Both add concrete evidence that the House restriction would strand prior investments and commitments."},{"child_excerpt":"I earnestly hope that the unfortunate amendments incorporated in H.R. 3790 will not be allowed to stand and that the funds requested by the Interior Department at the hearings of your subcommittee will be restored to the bill.","parent_excerpt":"I feel sure that ... the public housing limitations in the Independent Offices Appropriation Bill should be removed and the funds requested in the budget restored for the next fiscal year.","explanation":"The concluding requested remedy is nearly identical: remove the House limitation and restore the requested funds."}]}
